text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The newly-elected National Assembly (lower house) will meet on February 15 and the members will take oath the same day.
- Amin Fahim, nominee of Pakistan People's Party for Sindh chief ministership, said his party wanted a fresh dialogue with all political forces for a stable government.
- The long-awaited census is expected to be held in October.
- The government called for a gradual opening of trade with India by adding more items on the trade list.
- The Lahore High Court held that a citizen's right to go abroad is a fundamental one guaranteed by the constitution.

- Prime minister-elect Nawaz Sharif said his government will continue the economic reforms of the caretaker government and would also honour the deal with the International Monetary Fund as far as it is in the national interest.
- The new government will be sworn in on February 17.
- The new government will review energy pacts of previous government.
- The recent hike in the prices of furnace oil and gas have forced some cement factories to slash production by 50 percent.
- President Farooq Leghari held a 2-1/2-hour meeting with prime minister-elect Nawaz Sharif to discuss a range of issues, including the economy.
